MIND. [1] [Camph.]
Better when thinking of the existing complaint.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Camph.]
Throbbing, like beats with a hammer, in cerebellum, isochronous with pulse ; head hot, face red, limbs cool, > in standing ; mostly with such as were deprived of sexual intercourse.
Contraction as if laced together in cerebellum and glabella, with coldness all over. θ Cerebro-spinal meningitis.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Camph.]
Nose cold and pointed. θ Summer complaint. θ Cholera.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Camph.]
Cold sweat, with vomiting. θ Cholera.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Camph.]
Tongue cold, flabby, trembling.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Camph.]
Anxiety and restlessness, absence of evacuations, frequently chilly or feeling as if cold air was blowing on covered parts ; great sinking and collapse. θ Cholera Asiatica.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Camph.]
Burning during urination. θ Pregnancy.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Camph.]
Erethism of sexual system. θ Puerperal mania.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Camph.]
Newborn children ; asphyxia ; hard places in skin on abdomen and thighs, quickly increasing and getting harder, sometimes with a deep redness spreading nearly over whole abdomen and thighs ; violent fever, with startings and tetanic spasms, with bending backward ; make no water.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Camph.]
Influenza.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Camph.]
Cool breath, as from the grave, playing upon hand held before mouth. θ Cholera Asiatica.
   

COUGH. [27] [Camph.]
Congestion to chest.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Camph.]
Pulse : full ; weak ; not perceptible ; frequent and scarcely perceptible ; accelerated without fever ; very much accelerated, but undulating, and without strength ; very rapid ; full and rapid ; full and irritable ; irritable in evening ; hard or soft ; frequent and small (hepatized left lung) ; extremely small ; small and slow, sixty beats to minute ; small and hard, becoming slower and slower ; small, weak and quite frequent ; could not be counted ; extremely rapid and weak (typhus) ; audible and full ; weak and thready.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Camph.]
Coldness of limbs.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Camph.]
Very sensitive to cold air.
   

FEVER. [40] [Camph.]
Icy coldness all over, with deathlike paleness of face ; diminished circulation to parts most distant from heart.
Cold, clammy, weakening sweat.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Camph.]
Effects of shock from injury : surface of body cold, face pale and bluish, lips livid ; diarrhœa ; pulse feeble ; nervous anxiety and stupefaction, sighing respiration ; great exhaustion.
   

SKIN. [46] [Camph.]
All sequela of measles.
